scenario.title: Alstom Transport UK Ltd v London Underground Ltd
scenario.description: London Underground awarded contract to Bombardier for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment. Alstom challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. The challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. London Underground applied to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework, arguing that damages would be adequate remedy for Alstom if it succeeded at trial and that the balance of convenience favoured proceeding with the contract.

interests: Protection of Public Funds: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Critical AC traction motors and control equipment for London Underground's infrastructure
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence in the procurement process
goals: Defend the decision, maintain market relationships
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: The evaluation was conducted fairly and transparently, and we stand by our decision to award the contract to Bombardier.
legal_basis: Regulation 32(1) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £112.1 million contract value at stake
Fairness & Transparency: perceived injustice in applying technical threshold requirement
Protection of Reputation: maintain credibility with parent companies, shareholders and partners
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: Request immediate suspension of contract award to allow re-evaluation of bids

messages.message: We acknowledge Alstom's challenge and appreciate their diligence in bringing this matter to our attention. However, we would like to clarify whether Alstom is alleging that the technical threshold requirement was applied incorrectly or if there is a dispute over the interpretation of the evaluation criteria. Could you please provide more specificity on what you believe constitutes a manifest error in this instance?

We appreciate your clarification request and acknowledge that we did indeed challenge the application of the mandatory technical threshold requirement. However, we believe it's essential to clarify whether this was a genuine oversight or an intentional misapplication of the evaluation criteria. We would like to know if London Underground can provide more information on how they interpreted the technical threshold requirement in Bombardier's bid, specifically regarding the 'Technical Proposal' section (Section 3 of the tender document).

We appreciate Alstom's clarification request and acknowledge that we did indeed challenge the application of the mandatory technical threshold requirement. We would like to provide additional information on how we interpreted the technical threshold requirement in Bombardier's bid, specifically regarding the 'Technical Proposal' section (Section 3 of the tender document). Our evaluation team applied a score of 85% to this section, which met the minimum threshold of 80%. However, upon further review, we acknowledge that our initial scoring may have been overly generous. We are willing to revisit our scoring and provide additional feedback to Alstom.
messages.concession_made: We will revise our scoring and provide additional feedback to Alstom

messages.message: We appreciate London Underground's willingness to revisit their scoring and provide additional feedback. However, we are concerned that a score of 85% may still be overly generous considering Bombardier's bid did not meet all the mandatory technical threshold requirements. We would like to request that London Underground provides a detailed breakdown of how they arrived at this score, including any specific evaluation criteria or weighting applied. Furthermore, we would like to propose a joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) with a view to identifying any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement.
messages.proposal: Joint Review of Technical Proposal Section (Section 3)

messages.message: We appreciate Alstom's request for a detailed breakdown of our scoring and are willing to provide this information. However, we must clarify that we cannot disclose specific evaluation criteria or weighting applied to individual bidders without breaching commercial confidentiality. Nevertheless, we can confirm that our evaluation team applied the technical threshold requirement consistently across all bids, including Bombardier's. We also propose a joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) as suggested by Alstom, with the aim of identifying any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement.
messages.proposal: A joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3)

messages.message: We appreciate London Underground's willingness to provide a detailed breakdown of their scoring. However, we are concerned that a score of 85% may still be overly generous considering Bombardier's bid did not meet all the mandatory technical threshold requirements. We would like to propose a joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) with a view to identifying any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement. Furthermore, we request that London Underground provides a clear explanation for why they applied a score of 85% when their own evaluation team acknowledged that the initial scoring may have been overly generous.
messages.proposal: A joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) with a view to identifying any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement

messages.message: We acknowledge Alstom's concerns regarding the scoring of Bombardier's bid and the application of the technical threshold requirement. We are willing to provide a detailed breakdown of our evaluation process, including any specific evaluation criteria or weighting applied, while maintaining commercial confidentiality. However, we must clarify that our initial scoring may have been overly generous, and we are willing to revisit this aspect of the evaluation. Furthermore, we propose a joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) with Alstom's representatives to identify any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement.
messages.proposal: A joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) with Alstom's representatives
messages.concession_made: We are willing to revisit our scoring and provide additional feedback to Alstom

messages.message: We appreciate London Underground's willingness to provide a detailed breakdown of their scoring and revisit this aspect of the evaluation. However, we are concerned that the proposed joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) may not be sufficient to identify any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement. We propose that the joint review should include a thorough examination of the evaluation team's notes and documentation, as well as an independent review of Bombardier's bid by a third-party expert.
messages.proposal: A comprehensive joint review including evaluation team notes and documentation, and an independent review by a third-party expert

messages.message: We are willing to accept Alstom's proposal for a joint review of the Technical Proposal section (Section 3) with an independent third-party expert, as well as providing a thorough examination of our evaluation team's notes and documentation. We believe this will provide sufficient transparency and allow us to identify any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement. If this review confirms that Bombardier's bid did not meet all the mandatory technical threshold requirements, we are willing to re-evaluate the scoring and consider a revised award decision.
messages.concession_made: We will provide a thorough examination of our evaluation team's notes and documentation

messages.message: We appreciate London Underground's willingness to accept our proposal for a joint review with an independent third-party expert and provide a thorough examination of their evaluation team's notes and documentation. We believe this will provide sufficient transparency and allow us to identify any potential manifest errors in the application of the technical threshold requirement. If this review confirms that Bombardier's bid did not meet all the mandatory technical threshold requirements, we propose that London Underground re-evaluate the scoring and consider a revised award decision, potentially awarding the contract to Alstom or conducting a new evaluation process. We are willing to accept a partial award covering 50% of the contract value as a compromise, recognizing the importance of maintaining a fair and transparent procurement process.
messages.proposal: A partial award covering 50% of the contract value

ca_win_statement.win_statement: We have successfully navigated a complex dispute without resorting to costly and time-consuming legal action. This outcome demonstrates our commitment to transparency and fairness in procurement processes, while also protecting our interests.

summary.concessions_summary: Both parties made concessions throughout the negotiation, including London Underground's willingness to revisit their scoring, provide additional feedback, and conduct a joint review with Alstom's representatives. Alstom also proposed a partial award covering 50% of the contract value as a compromise.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively, focusing on whether the published criteria language was applied in a way that is rationally defensible and whether there were any manifest errors in the application of technical threshold requirements. The Court recommended continuing negotiation throughout the rounds, acknowledging that both parties' positions had merit.
summary.likely_next_steps: The negotiation reached a deadlock after Round 5, with no agreement on the contract award. Given the Court's assessments, it is likely that formal proceedings will be initiated to resolve the dispute, potentially involving an independent review of Bombardier's bid by a third-party expert and re-evaluation of the scoring.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation centered around Alstom's challenge to London Underground's evaluation process regarding the technical threshold requirement. Both parties made concessions, but ultimately failed to reach an agreement on the contract award. The Court assessed each round qualitatively, recommending continued negotiation until a deadlock was reached. Formal proceedings are now likely to ensue.
